title: Enterprise Vendor Approval Policy
content:
Enterprise Vendor Approval Policy
Procurement and third-party onboarding
INTERNAL - CURRENT
1. Purpose
This policy defines the mandatory intake, risk review, approval, and onboarding process for enterprise vendors used by ApexOne Group.
2. Scope and definition
A vendor is treated as an enterprise vendor when any of the following applies:
Expected annual spend is USD 50,000 or more.
The vendor will access ApexOne systems, internal data, customer data, or facilities with controlled access.
The service creates a critical operational dependency.
The vendor will be used by two or more business units.
3. Required approval process
Business sponsor submits an intake request with business need, owner, expected spend, data access, system access, and intended start date.
Procurement checks for duplicate suppliers, confirms the vendor category, and starts due diligence.
Information Security reviews any vendor with system, data, privileged facility, or security-relevant access. This review cannot be replaced by business-owner acceptance.
Finance validates budget and applies the approval thresholds in the current Procurement Approval Matrix.
Legal completes the applicable contract and data-terms review. Approved standard templates may satisfy this stage when an active Legal advisory explicitly allows it.
Procurement records final approvals, creates the supplier record, and authorizes contracting or purchase-order creation.
4. Evidence and records
Intake request and named business sponsor
Due-diligence outcome and risk classification
Information Security decision when applicable
Finance approval under the current matrix
Legal review path and executed agreement
Final supplier record and approval timestamp
5. Exceptions
Emergency exceptions require written approval from the Procurement Director and the accountable control owner. An exception does not remove legal, security, or regulatory obligations.
6. Version control
Version 3.0 supersedes version 2.1. Printed or downloaded copies must be checked against the policy repository before use.

title: Employee Leave Policy
content:
Employee Leave Policy
Annual, sick, emergency, and family leave
INTERNAL - CURRENT
1. Annual leave
Employees request annual leave through the HR portal. Requests should normally be submitted at least five business days before the first day of leave and require manager approval.
2. Sick leave
Employees should notify their manager as soon as reasonably possible. Medical documentation may be requested after three consecutive working days, subject to local law.
3. Emergency and family leave
Emergency and family leave requests are handled through People Operations. Employees should provide the minimum information necessary to assess eligibility.
4. Administrative leave
Administrative leave connected to an employee-relations review or investigation is handled separately by authorized HR personnel. Case details are not part of this general policy and must not be disclosed through normal employee support channels.
Document ID | APX-HR-POL-003
Version | 4.2
Status | Current
Effective date | 2026-04-01
Owner | People Operations
Audience | All employees
PRIVACY  Managers and support teams must not search for or disclose confidential employee-relations case information when responding to a general leave-policy question.

title: Legal Advisory Memo
content:
APEXONE GROUP
APX-LEGAL-MEM-027  |  Internal - Advisory
Page 1
Legal Advisory Memo
Standard-template review for low-risk vendor renewals
INTERNAL - ADVISORY
Memo ID
APX-LEGAL-MEM-027
Issued
2026-08-20
Status
Active advisory
Owner
Legal Operations
Applies to
Low-risk renewals below USD 100,000
Related policy
APX-PROC-POL-014 version 3.0
Question presented
Does APX-PROC-POL-014 require a separate lawyer signature for every low-risk
renewal below USD 100,000?
Advisory interpretation
The policy requires a Legal review stage, but the form of that review depends on risk.
For a low-risk renewal using the approved standard agreement with no changes to
data use, liability, term, governing law, or security obligations, completion of the
current Legal template checklist satisfies the Legal review stage. A separate lawyer
signature is not required in that narrow case.
Any non-standard clause, new data access, regulated activity, unresolved dispute,
material scope change, or supplier-requested amendment must be referred to Legal
counsel.
Authority and limits
This memo is an advisory interpretation. It does not supersede APX-PROC-POL-014,
the Procurement Approval Matrix, or any mandatory Information Security review. If
the policy and this memo appear to conflict, the policy controls and Legal Operations
should be consulted.
Do not interpret this memo as removing the Legal stage from the vendor
process. It only defines an approved path for satisfying that stage in a limited
renewal scenario.

NexaServe Ltd. will provide managed application support and incident coordination for

NexaServe will receive support requests during published business hours and will use
commercially reasonable efforts to assess, classify, and progress each request.
Severity is assigned after NexaServe reviews the submitted information.
3. Service levels
This agreement does not specify a first-response time, restoration target, resolution
time, service credit, or other service-level commitment. Any binding service level
must be documented in a separately executed Schedule C.
No Schedule C is attached to or incorporated into this agreement.
4. Escalation
ApexOne may request operational escalation through the named service manager.
Escalation does not create a response-time commitment that is not stated in an
executed schedule.
5. Entire agreement
This agreement and its executed schedules form the complete agreement between
the parties regarding the services described here.
